_about: Regulatory clauses per KB finding code (#269). Hand-written and reviewed: one row per code. 'clauses' are the clauses the finding always breaks (or whose obligation it always triggers, e.g. the post-quantum migration clauses for quantum-vulnerable public-key cryptography, CERT-In 8.4.1.6 VEX for a published vulnerability); 'rules' add clauses only when the asset's evidence matches 'match' (case-insensitive), e.g. TDEA only when Triple DES is named. The evidence is algorithm names only (#289): the algorithms the classifier flagged for the code (classify._Out algorithms) and the asset's algorithm, never its name, location or a sentence; when no algorithm was recorded every rule's clauses are cited with a note saying so. 'match_from' reads the pattern (a regex or a set of names) from the classifier source (path:NAME) instead of repeating it; 'unless' excludes names that match it. 'notes' attach an explanation to one clause of the row. A code that breaks no clause of a framework is not cited under it. Clause keys are those of kb_compliance.CLAUSES. build_kb.py copies clauses and rules (match, clauses) into each entry as 'clauses' / 'clause_rules', and fails on a missing or extra row, an unknown clause key, a row without a basis, or a rule whose pattern does not match its example.

AT_REST_ENCRYPTION_WEAK.basis: a legacy cipher or provider default where a customer key is required: not strong encryption at rest (SEBI); data is still encrypted, so RBI 106 / CERT-In 7.1 hold

CERT_SELF_SIGNED.basis: a certificate clients do not trust is not a valid TLS certificate (CERT-In 6.1.7)

CUSTOM_CRYPTO.basis: a home-made cipher or hash is not an internationally accepted, published standard (RBI) nor an industry-standard algorithm (SEBI Annexure-H item 5)

DOWNGRADE_PROTECTION_MISSING.basis: no downgrade protection: not a strict TLS configuration

EOL_BASE_IMAGE.basis: an end-of-life or bundled component is not a vulnerability record: CERT-In 8.4.1.6 (VEX) applies only once a vulnerability is published, and no other clause in the knowledge base covers support status

EOL_CRYPTO_LIBRARY.basis: an end-of-life or bundled component is not a vulnerability record: CERT-In 8.4.1.6 (VEX) applies only once a vulnerability is published, and no other clause in the knowledge base covers support status

EXPIRED_CERTIFICATE.basis: expired: not renewed in time and not a valid certificate

HARDCODED_KEY.basis: a key embedded in source: key storage methodology (SEBI Annexure-H item 5)

KMS_KEY_DELETION_UNPROTECTED.basis: key or certificate lifecycle hygiene (rotation, deletion protection, inventory): no clause in the knowledge base requires it, so it is not cited under any framework

KMS_KEY_POLICY_PUBLIC.basis: any principal may use the key: key storage methodology

KMS_KEY_ROTATION_DISABLED.basis: key or certificate lifecycle hygiene (rotation, deletion protection, inventory): no clause in the knowledge base requires it, so it is not cited under any framework

KNOWN_TLS_VULNERABILITY.basis: a named TLS vulnerability: a protocol configuration demonstrated to be vulnerable (RBI, CERT-In 8.4.2.2) and a VEX status is due (CERT-In 8.4.1.6)

LIBRARY_CVE_RANGE.basis: a crypto component with a published vulnerability: VEX status due

PLAINTEXT_LISTENER.basis: a listener without TLS: data in transit not protected; RBI: each entity type's own data-in-transit paragraph (CB 106, SFB/PB/AIFI/CIC 105, UCB 23, NBFC 118)

PROVIDER_MANAGED_KEY.basis: the data is encrypted at rest; a customer-managed key is better practice, not a clause requirement

QUANTUM_VULNERABLE.basis: RSA / EC / DH public-key cryptography: the post-quantum migration clauses

REUSED_NONCE.basis: nonce reuse with an approved cipher (GCM, CTR, CBC) is a configuration demonstrated to be insecure (it leaks the XOR of the plaintexts and, in GCM, the authentication key), the same basis as ECB (WEAK_CIPHER_MODE): RBI; the cipher itself may be strong, so no SEBI clause

SELF_SIGNED_LEAF.basis: a self-signed leaf is not a valid TLS certificate for clients

STATIC_IV.basis: IV reuse with an approved cipher (GCM, CTR, CBC) is a configuration demonstrated to be insecure (it leaks the XOR of the plaintexts and, in GCM, the authentication key), the same basis as ECB (WEAK_CIPHER_MODE): RBI; the cipher itself may be strong, so no SEBI clause

STATIC_SALT.basis: a constant salt in a password-based key derivation is a configuration demonstrated to be insecure (one precomputed table or guessing run serves every password; NIST SP 800-132 section 5.1 requires a random salt), the same basis as a reused IV (STATIC_IV): RBI; the KDF itself may be an approved one, so no SEBI clause

TLS_VERIFICATION_DISABLED.basis: certificate chains are not checked (CERT-In 8.4.2.2) so the TLS connection is not secure (CERT-In 6.2.7); encryption itself is still in place

UNENCRYPTED_AT_REST.basis: no encryption at rest; RBI: each entity type's own data-at-rest paragraph (CB 106, SFB/PB/AIFI/CIC 105, UCB 120 for Level II and above, NBFC 95(4) secure storage)

UNENCRYPTED_IN_TRANSIT.basis: no TLS: data in transit not protected; RBI: each entity type's own data-in-transit paragraph (CB 106, SFB/PB/AIFI/CIC 105, UCB 23, NBFC 118)

VULNERABLE_CRYPTO_LIBRARY.basis: a crypto component with a published advisory: VEX status due

WEAK_ALGORITHM.basis: a broken or deprecated algorithm (RBI). Algorithm-specific clauses follow the evidence: TDEA for 3DES, SEBI for weak ciphers, SHA-1 signatures only for a SHA-1 signature algorithm, 112-bit for small public keys

rules.basis: the evidence names Triple DES (TDEA): SP 800-131A Table 1 disallows three-key TDEA for encryption after 2023, and SEBI asks for strong encryption algorithms
the evidence names a broken or deprecated encryption cipher (DES, 3DES, RC4, RC2, NULL, EXPORT, Blowfish, IDEA, CAST): SEBI Annexure-H item 5 asks for strong encryption algorithms
a SHA-1 signature algorithm: SP 800-131A Table 8

rules.example: Undersized asymmetric key on RSA: 1024-bit is below the 2048-bit floor
rules.basis: a public key below 112-bit security (SP 800-131A): RSA/DSA/DH under 2048 bits or an EC key under 224 bits, also as the code scanner words it ("RSA: 1024-bit")

WEAK_CERTIFICATE_KEY.basis: a certificate key below RSA 2048 / EC 224: below 112-bit security

WEAK_CERTIFICATE_SIGNATURE.basis: an MD5 or SHA-1 certificate signature: deprecated (RBI), not valid for clients (CERT-In 6.1.7); SHA-1 signature generation only when SHA-1 is named

rules.basis: a SHA-1 signature: SP 800-131A Table 8

WEAK_CIPHER_MODE.basis: ECB is demonstrated to be insecure for multi-block data (RBI); the cipher itself may be strong, so no SEBI clause

WEAK_CIPHER_SUITE.basis: weak suites or legacy SSH / IKE algorithms configured (CERT-In 8.4.2.2, RBI); SEBI and TDEA follow the ciphers the evidence names

rules.basis: the evidence names a broken or deprecated encryption cipher (DES, 3DES, RC4, RC2, NULL, EXPORT, Blowfish, IDEA, CAST): SEBI Annexure-H item 5 asks for strong encryption algorithms
the evidence names Triple DES (TDEA): SP 800-131A Table 1 disallows three-key TDEA for encryption after 2023, and SEBI asks for strong encryption algorithms

WEAK_KDF_ITERATIONS.basis: an iteration count below the published minimum for the KDF is a configuration that does not follow internationally accepted guidance and is demonstrated to be insecure against offline guessing: below 1,000 for Java PBE (NIST SP 800-132 section 5.2), below 100,000 for .NET Rfc2898DeriveBytes, whose default is 1,000 (Microsoft CA5387, OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet: 600,000 for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256): RBI; the KDF itself may be an approved one, so no SEBI clause

WEAK_KEY_SIZE.basis: a key below the minimum size (RBI key length); the 112-bit clause only for public keys the evidence names

rules.example: Undersized asymmetric key on RSA: 1024-bit is below the 2048-bit floor
rules.basis: a public key below 112-bit security (SP 800-131A): RSA/DSA/DH under 2048 bits or an EC key under 224 bits, also as the code scanner words it ("RSA: 1024-bit")

WEAK_PADDING.basis: RSA encryption with PKCS#1 v1.5 (or no) padding: SP 800-131A Sec. 6 Table 5 disallows PKCS#1 v1.5 key transport

WEAK_PROTOCOL.basis: SSLv3, TLS 1.0/1.1, SSH-1 or IKEv1: deprecated protocols; SEBI Annexure-I only for SSL/TLS

rules.basis: a deprecated SSL/TLS version is not strong transport encryption

WEAK_RNG.basis: a non-cryptographic generator for key material is an algorithm demonstrated to be insecure

WEAK_RSA_EXPONENT.basis: RSA keys with public exponent 3 are outside the published standard (FIPS 186-5 requires 2^16 < e < 2^256) and demonstrated to be insecure (Bleichenbacher's e = 3 signature forgery, cube-root recovery of small unpadded messages): RBI; RSA itself with e = 65537 is an approved algorithm, so no SEBI clause
